correctness.rationale: The prescribed C(a+t,t), evaluated at the lower displacement ε and the reflected upper displacement 1−a−ε, bounds both ε-corner masses by ε(a+ε). For sharpness the lower-square replacement at mixing weight ℓ/a preserves both marginals; every prescribed rectangle includes its entire horizontal span, so the section is unchanged. The intermediate law is symmetric, so its restriction to the upper square has identical coordinate marginals ν. The upper replacement couples ν to itself by the diagonal pushforward of ν, mixed at weight u/a. This is a finite measure of total mass ν([0,1]), not its normalized probability law: equivalently, the record's finite-mass quantile pushforward uses Lebesgue measure on (0,m), or multiplies the uniform probability law there by m. For ε<min(a,1−a), each upper terminal strip retains marginal mass aε, unchanged by the first patch, and the terminal corner mass changes from ε² to aε under the diagonal coupling. The second patch does not touch the lower ε-corner or the section for t<1−a; the endpoint is fixed by C(1,1−a)=1−a. This verifies both tail limits for every pair simultaneously even when the squares overlap. The checker source was inspected; the frozen reported 26,912 grid assertions are consistency evidence and were not executed or used to infer the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: A complete feasible region gives more information than two separate sharp upper bounds. The result resolves the non-identifiability of both asymptotic tail masses under an exact continuum of independence-section data, identifies the sharp simultaneous endpoint, and shows that overlapping corner squares do not impose a tradeoff. Its construction works across the natural full range 0<a<1.
